name: WebView loadUrl/evaluateJavascript with string concatenation
attack_scenario: userName is set to `');stealToken();//`; the concatenated javascript: URL breaks out of the string literal and runs attacker JS in the app's WebView origin, reaching any exposed bridge.
negative_test_hint: set userName to "');stealToken();//" and assert it reaches the WebView as an inert JSON-encoded value, never as executable script

exemplar.explanation: Concatenating untrusted data into a javascript: URL or an evaluateJavascript/loadData string injects it into a script context inside the WebView, giving DOM-based XSS in the app's own origin; if a native bridge exists this escalates to native calls. Passing data as a JSON-encoded value to a fixed JS function keeps user input out of the script body (CWE-79 / OWASP MASVS-CODE).
